issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of a summary application for mortgage redemption does not bar a later civil suit for redemption when the suit does not seek to reopen an adjudication of the underlying mortgage right and is filed within the ordinary limitation period.
material_facts: The mortgagor applied for summary redemption, agreed to pay the amount determined in a compromise, and the Collector dismissed the applications after the mortgagor defaulted on payment.
The mortgagor’s successors later filed civil suits seeking redemption and accepted the amount determined in the summary proceedings rather than challenging that determination.
The civil suits were within the limitation period applicable to ordinary mortgage-redemption suits, though they were brought more than one year after the Collector’s orders.
issues.conclusion: The one-year period for challenging an order under the Punjab Act did not bar the civil suits. The Collector’s orders were conclusive as to what they decided, but the suits sought redemption rather than the setting aside of those orders; the suits were within ordinary limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12 and 13 of the Redemption of Mortgages (Punjab) Act, 1913 make an order conclusive as to the matters decided and bar a further application under that Act, but do not extinguish the ordinary civil remedy of redemption. Article 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908, equivalent to Article 100 of the Limitation Act, 1963, applies to a suit to set aside an official order, not to a suit that does not challenge the order’s adjudication. The ordinary limitation provisions for redemption govern a civil suit seeking redemption and possession. The Court relied on Tulsi Dass @ Nirmal Das v. Diala Ram and Sheo Lal v. Sultan, which distinguish an order’s substance from its form and hold that a dismissal which does not adjudicate the underlying right need not be set aside before a redemption suit is brought.

predicates.civil_suit_for_mortgage_redemption: A party brought a civil suit seeking redemption of a mortgage.
predicates.prior_summary_redemption_application_dis: A summary application seeking redemption of the mortgage was dismissed.
predicates.suit_does_not_seek_to_reopen_underlying_: The civil suit seeks redemption without asking the court to set aside or reconsider an adjudication of the underlying mortgage right.
predicates.suit_within_ordinary_limitation: The civil suit was filed within the limitation period applicable to an ordinary claim for mortgage redemption.

issues.definition: When a civil mortgage-redemption suit follows dismissal of a summary application, it is maintainable if it does not seek to reopen an underlying adjudication and is within ordinary limitation.

issues.legal_issue: Equitable principles of mortgage redemption may be applied by a civil court even when the statutory provision governing redemption does not apply in the jurisdiction.
material_facts: The suits sought redemption of mortgages and recovery of the mortgaged property.
The Transfer of Property Act provision on redemption did not apply in the jurisdiction at the relevant time.
The Court found that the principles governing redemption in that provision were consistent with justice, equity and good conscience.
issues.conclusion: Although the statutory provision did not apply per se, its principles applied as rules of justice, equity and good conscience, and the civil court had jurisdiction to grant decrees of redemption.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principles of justice, equity and good conscience to recognize the right of redemption reflected in Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, notwithstanding that the Act did not apply per se. It relied on Mussammat Bhagwan Devi v. Mussammat Bunyadi Khanum, Safdar Ali v. Ghulam Mohi-ud-din, Mian Nizam & Din Mohammad v. Lala Ram Sukh Das, Milkha Singh v. Mst. Shankari, M/s Ram Gopal Dula Singh v. Sardar Gurbux Singh Jiwan Singh, Atma Singh & Gian Singh v. Mangal Singh, and Ganeshi Lal v. Jyoti Pershad; it also referred to Suryanarayan v. Sriramulu.

predicates.civil_suit_for_mortgage_redemption: A party brought a civil suit seeking redemption of a mortgage.
predicates.statutory_redemption_rule_not_applicable: The statutory rule specifically governing mortgage redemption did not apply in the jurisdiction.
predicates.mortgage_redemption_principle_consistent: The principle recognizing redemption of the mortgage is consistent with justice, equity and good conscience.

issues.definition: If a civil suit seeks mortgage redemption, the statutory redemption rule does not apply, and the redemption principle is consistent with equity, the civil court may decree redemption.
